To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the online processing of written text is a complex process in which many cognitive processes are involved and (2) these processes can be measured with a variety of methods, such as reading times, eye movements, and event-related potentials.

the online processing of a text is a dynamic process in which a reader continuously integrates new information with the current knowledge base and that the online processes of reading are related to offline processes of text comprehension.

(i) the processing of written text is a highly interactive and dynamic process; (ii) the reader’s knowledge plays a key role in the processing of written texts, and (iii) the reader’s task goals and reading strategies have a strong impact on the processing of written language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive processes underlying the comprehension of written text.
the question of how children learn from text and how they process written information.
the cognitive processes underlying the online processing of written text.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence on whether the cognitive processing of texts by children and adults is similar or different.
the development of the ability to comprehend text is a complex process that is influenced by many factors.
there is no conclusive evidence on the development of the processes underlying online processing in text comprehension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have tried to provide a framework for understanding the cognitive processes involved in the comprehension of text.
we have shown the importance of the reader’s knowledge in understanding a text and how this can be measured.
the development of text comprehension is not a straightforward process of increasing cognitive skills but that children’s learning of text is embedded in a social and cultural environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of text comprehension skills is not only a matter of increasing knowledge and skills, but also of developing the ability to use them flexibly in different contexts.
the development of text comprehension is not a linear, one-way process.
there are important differences between children's and adults' text comprehension processes, which are not only quantitative but also qualitative in nature.
